notes: The MIDI jack is drawn sitting on top of the breadboard with short coloured leads going into it. I modelled those leads as two short jumper wires (wire2 and wire3), each joined to a jack pin. The jack itself is not plugged into the breadboard.
Pin mapping follows the text and schematic. MIDI pin 5 goes through a 220 ohm resistor to digital pin 1 (TX). MIDI pin 4 goes through a 220 ohm resistor to 5V. MIDI pin 2 goes to GND.

The breadboard uses the catalogue naming: 't' is rows a-e and 'b' is rows f-j. The image labels the top half j-f and the bottom half e-a. I followed the catalogue and placed the resistors across the centre gap in columns 7 and 9.
The black wire lands on the Uno GND header pin next to AREF. I used GND.1 because the catalogue does not say which of GND.1-3 that is.
The manual says to use Serial1 instead of Serial on ATmega32U4 boards (Leonardo). The image shows an Uno, so I built the Uno version.
